q: If a body is dropped from a height near the earth's surface, the body will fall with a ____.
e: If a body is dropped from a height near the earth's surface, the body will fall with a constant acceleration g. Constant acceleration g here means how quickly velocity changes. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: If the ____ is neglected, the fall of the body is defined as free fall.
e: If the air resistance is neglected, the fall of the body is defined as free fall. By definition that quantity is air resistance.

q: Equation of motion under ____ described in chapter 2 can be used in the free fall.
e: Equation of motion under constant acceleration described in chapter 2 can be used in the free fall. Constant acceleration here means how quickly velocity changes. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: In these equations we will use the symbol ____ for displacement s and g for acceleration a.
e: In these equations we will use the symbol h for displacement s and g for acceleration a. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: Hence, the equations become $v = v_0 + gt$ and ____
e: Hence, the equations become $v = v_0 + gt$ and $v^2 = v_0^2 + 2gh$. The physics in this sentence is built around $v^2 = v_0^2 + 2gh$.

q: Note that the acceleration due to gravity g is directed ____ (towards the centre of the earth).
e: Note that the acceleration due to gravity g is directed downwards (towards the centre of the earth). Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: Since acceleration g is always directed downwards its value will be ____ (i.e. $g = -9.8 \text{ ms}^{-2}$).
e: Since acceleration g is always directed downwards its value will be negative (i.e. $g = -9.8 \text{ ms}^{-2}$). Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.
